headline_hook: OpenAI Ships GPT Live, Grok 4.5 Lands, and Mistral Steers Into Robotics
preview_topics: the GPT Live and Grok 4.5 arms race
why in-person finals exposed an AI competence gap

pick_of_the_day.thesis: The 50% score collapse doesn't just prove students are cheating — it reveals that AI-assisted learning creates an illusion of competence that universities, employers, and the entire credentialing system have no framework to detect or address.

model_literacy.relevance: With Grok 4.5, SWE-1.7, and OpenAI all claiming SOTA this week, OpenAI's own paper on separating signal from noise in coding evals gives readers the lens to evaluate which claims hold up and which are cherry-picked slices.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT Live — real-time AI gets its own product line
items.angle: OpenAI bets that real-time voice-and-video interaction is a distinct enough use case to warrant a standalone product, not just a ChatGPT feature — positioning against every live AI assistant on the market.
items.key_fact: First standalone product line from OpenAI outside the GPT/ChatGPT family

items.title: xAI drops Grok 4.5 with massive community reception
items.angle: Another frontier model in a week already packed with releases — the cadence itself is the story, as the gap between major model drops shrinks from months to days.
items.key_fact: 432 likes and 467 RTs on Hacker News

items.title: Mistral enters robotics with Robostral Navigate
items.angle: A text-and-code lab building a dedicated robotics navigation model signals that frontier labs see embodied AI as the next competitive moat — not just another benchmark category.
items.key_fact: 392 likes on HN — strong developer signal for specialized robotics models from frontier labs

items.title: Cognition's SWE-1.7 claims it's closing in on GPT 5.5 and Opus
items.angle: The Devin team benchmarking against frontier models — not other agents — reframes the coding agent race as model-tier competition, and the community's 244 likes suggest they're buying it.
items.key_fact: Claims near GPT 5.5 and Opus performance on coding tasks

items.title: OpenAI publishes a framework for separating signal from noise in coding evals
items.angle: A meta-evaluation paper from the lab with the most to gain from rigorous benchmarking — read it as both methodology and strategy document.
items.key_fact: 126 likes, 55 RTs — community wants better eval methodology

items.title: NVIDIA and HuggingFace lay out open data requirements for agents
items.angle: Agent training data is fundamentally different from chat data — this collaboration defines what that actually means for the open-source stack.
items.key_fact: Joint NVIDIA-HuggingFace open data initiative specifically for agent training and evaluation

items.title: HuggingFace transformers becomes a native-speed vLLM backend
items.angle: The performance penalty for using transformers models in production inference is gone — this unifies research and production into one pipeline.
items.key_fact: Native-speed modeling backend eliminates the transformers-to-vLLM performance gap

items.title: Microsoft open-sources Flint, a visualization language built for AI agents
items.angle: Agents can write code but producing clean charts has been a persistent weak spot — Flint gives them a DSL purpose-built for data viz.
items.key_fact: 167 likes on Show HN — fills a real gap in agent tooling

items.title: CrewAI 1.15.2 ships inline skills and dynamic model selection
items.angle: Inline skill definitions remove a major friction point in multi-agent orchestration — define capabilities right where you use them.
items.key_fact: New inline skills, dynamic LLM model selection wizard, and Flow Definition authoring

items.title: Thomson Reuters shows what enterprise AI adoption actually looks like in regulated industries
items.angle: One of the most conservative enterprise customers detailing how they build with Claude for legal and tax — the gap between AI demos and production in regulated industries, closed.
items.key_fact: Production Claude deployment in legal and tax workflows at Thomson Reuters

items.title: Modal's CTO argues AI infrastructure must be rebuilt for agents
items.angle: Request-response infrastructure breaks under long-running, stateful, bursty agent workloads — Modal has two years of receipts to prove it.
items.key_fact: Latent Space follow-up two years after Modal's first appearance, now with production data on agent infra patterns

items.title: Brown professor's in-person final experiment: scores drop 50% without AI
items.angle: The most concrete data point yet on the gap between AI-assisted and unassisted student performance — and universities have no playbook for what comes next.
items.key_fact: Exam scores fell 50% when students couldn't use AI tools

items.title: Anthropic's marketing ops team shows how they actually use Cowork
items.angle: Anthropic eating its own dogfood — specific workflows for automated reporting and campaign builds, not just 'we use AI internally.'
items.key_fact: Detailed playbook for marketing ops automation with Claude Cowork

items.title: Lilian Weng's 35-paper harness engineering taxonomy, distilled
items.angle: Latent Space condenses the comprehensive RSI harness survey into actionable takeaways — a practical companion to yesterday's deep dive.
items.key_fact: 35 papers on self-improvement harness engineering condensed into one read

items.title: Fable Advisor: an open-source multi-model orchestrator using Claude Fable as the router
items.angle: A practical answer to 'which model for which task' — Fable as the meta-orchestrator that routes across Opus, GPT, and Sonnet by complexity.
items.key_fact: 152 likes — uses Claude Fable to route tasks across multiple frontier models

items.title: Rabbithole turns learning into an infinite canvas with MCP support
items.angle: Select text, ask questions, and answers branch out as navigable documents — works as an MCP server for Claude Code and Codex, bridging research and coding.
items.key_fact: 134 likes — MCP-native learning tool compatible with Claude Code and Codex

quick_links.title: Claude Code v2.1.205 fixes silent schema failures and transcript tampering
quick_links.angle: The --json-schema fix alone will save teams debugging phantom failures
quick_links.key_fact: Blocks transcript tampering in auto mode, fixes schema output and max-turns message loss

quick_links.title: Claude Code v2.1.204 fixes hook streaming for headless sessions
quick_links.angle: Prevents remote agents from being idle-reaped mid-hook in CI/CD
quick_links.key_fact: SessionStart hook events now stream correctly in headless mode

quick_links.title: sqlite-migrate 0.2 ships schema migration tooling for the SQLite ecosystem
quick_links.angle: Simon Willison expands the sqlite-utils companion toolkit

quick_links.title: Onboard-CLI: AST-based codebase visualization powered by LLMs
quick_links.angle: Visual maps of unfamiliar codebases — addresses the onboarding pain point
quick_links.key_fact: LLM-powered AST analysis generates navigable codebase maps

quick_links.title: github-code web component embeds syntax-highlighted snippets without iframes
quick_links.angle: Clean solution to the 'show code in blog posts' problem — no API keys needed
quick_links.key_fact: Zero-dependency web component for embedding GitHub code
